evidence: Mentioned changing career to ML due to 'hype' but immediately contextualized this with the 'tough' reality of learning to code for 'hours and hours' and facing discouragement.

Explicitly states: 'I will not says I'm good at machine learning. I know because I had built so many times so many errors and after so many stacks you learn something.' This directly contrasts idealized capability with imperfect, iterative learning.
strength: Strong - Provides a clear personal narrative of initial attraction via hype vs. the gritty reality of skill acquisition.

evidence: Describes facing and diagnosing model bias in an astronomy project: 'it underestimates some of the classes... It is some kind of model bias I guess.' Shows an understanding of imperfect system behavior without expressing shock or eroded trust; it's presented as a technical problem to be understood.
strength: Moderate - Acknowledges unsatisfactory behavior but frames it as a known challenge within the field, not a betrayal of trust.

evidence: Discusses model bias not as a black-box frustration, but as a technical characteristic of a chosen algorithm ('I had to choose one algorithm, but it was not...'). The 'deficit' is presented more as a trade-off or limitation than an opaque mystery.
strength: Weak - The focus is on algorithmic choice and performance trade-offs, not on a user's frustration with a lack of interpretable decision-making.

evidence: Describes personal experience with model bias ('underestimates some of the classes'). While this is a technical description of unfair *output*, Person 2 does not express this as a reason to reject the AI/ML field. It is a problem encountered within her work.
strength: Weak - Presents bias as an encountered and accepted technical hurdle within a project, not as a fundamental barrier to adoption or use.

metaphors_identified.metaphor: Career Path as a Hype-Driven Wave
metaphors_identified.quote: machine learning started to make hype and I decided... to make a career change
metaphors_identified.interpretation: Person 2 metaphorically describes the rise of ML as a force ('hype') that influenced her life direction. This aligns with the external societal perception of AI as a powerful, attractive trend.

metaphors_identified.quote: after so many stacks you learn something
metaphors_identified.interpretation: Implies knowledge is built incrementally, like layers or stacks, often through failure ('errors'). This counters the 'Magic Box' idea of innate, flawless intelligence.

metaphors_identified.quote: talking with different country people... was make me feel uplifted
metaphors_identified.interpretation: Diversity is not just a logistical reality but an active, positive force that elevates mood and perspective. This extends beyond AI to team dynamics.

metaphors_identified.quote: I was stuck... I stuck summer... help me to overcome this problem
metaphors_identified.interpretation: Describes technical challenges as states of immobilization ('stuck'), with solutions coming from collaborative support to become mobile again ('overcome'). Highlights the non-magical, effortful process of development.

negative_cases_identified.case: Absence of 'Magic Box' or Anthropomorphic Projection
negative_cases_identified.description: Person 2 consistently describes AI/ML in technical, non-magical terms: as algorithms with biases, code with errors, and skills built through practice. There is no indication she expects human-like reasoning or infallibility. Her expectations are shaped by hands-on experience, not hype.
supporting_quotes: "I had built so many times so many errors."
"It underestimates some of the classes... It is some kind of model bias."

negative_cases_identified.case: No Evidence of 'Feedback Dissonance' or 'Trust Erosion'
negative_cases_identified.description: While Person 2 discusses project failures and irresponsible leaders, these are attributed to human factors (personal issues, lack of qualification) or technical challenges, not to a gap between unrealistic AI expectations and reality. There is no mention of users filing bug reports based on flawed benchmarks or disillusionment with AI pilots.
supporting_quotes: "The problem is that [she was] not qualified to lead."
"This is not cultural... we may have to feel threatened, and this is not cultural."

negative_cases_identified.case: Utility Mismatch is a Technical, Not Expectational, Problem
negative_cases_identified.description: When discussing model bias (where AI output doesn't align with the goal of accurate classification for all classes), Person 2 frames it as a standard research dilemma involving algorithm selection and trade-offs. It is not presented as a surprising failure of AI to read her mind or align with organizational goals.
